mainTopic: Festival rejoicing, dividing offerings between שלמים and עולות, and bringing leftover חגיגה animals on later days
overview: The amud opens by finishing a דרשה on 'ושמחת בחגך': only animals that can be brought as a חגיגה count for festival rejoicing, so birds and מנחות are left out. רב אשי learns the same rule from 'ושמחת' alone, and uses 'בחגך' for רב's rule that one does not marry during the מועד. A new משנה then explains how to split festival offerings between שלמים and עולות, depending on how many people one has to feed and how much money one has. The גמרא asks how a poor person can bring many שלמים. רב חסדא answers that he combines his money with מעשר שני money to buy a big bull. רב ששת adds that one may even combine and bring more animals, and the גמרא uses a ברייתא about 'the first eating' to show his view can stand. Finally, ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about whether leftover חגיגה animals may be brought on a later day of the festival. רבי אבא explains that they are speaking about different cases: whether or not the person said his plan from the start. The גמרא proves this from two reports of רבי יוחנן and begins bringing a third report, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only animals fit for a חגיגה count for festival rejoicing
steps.stepSummary: The previous דרשה ends: the word 'בחגך' teaches that festival rejoicing comes through animals that can be brought as a חגיגה, so birds and מנחות are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rejoicing comes through those animals from which a חגיגה can be brought. This leaves out things from which a חגיגה cannot be brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that began before this section. It explains which offerings count for the מצוה of rejoicing on the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בחגך' (in your festival) is read as 'with your חגיגה offering'. So only the kinds of offerings that can be a חגיגה, meaning cattle and sheep, fulfill the rejoicing. Birds and מנחות can never be a חגיגה, so they are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival שלמים offering brought on the רגל
Can come from them (can be brought from this type)
Are excluded, are left out

phrases.english: Those from which the festival offering can come,
phrases.notes: This finishes the דרשה on 'בחגך' from before. He means animals: cattle and sheep.

phrases.english: excluded are these
phrases.notes: He means birds and flour offerings.

phrases.english: from which the festival offering cannot come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a דרשה begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Festival rejoicing is fulfilled only with animals that can serve as a חגיגה. Birds and מנחות are excluded.

steps.title: רב אשי derives the rule from 'ושמחת' instead
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the exclusion of birds and מנחות comes from the word 'ושמחת' itself, since they bring no real joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We learn it from 'and you shall rejoice'. That leaves out things that have no joy in them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different source for the same rule. He does not need the word 'בחגך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה stays the same: birds and מנחות do not count. Only the source changes. Eating them is not true festive joy, so the word 'ושמחת' already leaves them out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived, it comes out of
'And you shall rejoice' (from the פסוק)
Joy, rejoicing

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not arguing about the הלכה. Both sides agree birds and מנחות are excluded. They only argue about which word in the פסוק teaches it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is derived from 'and you shall rejoice.'
Excluded are these, which have no joy in them.
phrases.notes: Birds and flour offerings again. Eating them doesn't give the joy that meat does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same rule as step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exclusion of birds and מנחות comes from 'ושמחת', because they have no real שמחה.

steps.title: What does רב אשי learn from 'בחגך'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רב אשי does not use 'בחגך' for this rule, what does that word teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי, what does he do with this word 'בחגך'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a standard question. Every word in the פסוק should teach something, so what is 'בחגך' for according to רב אשי? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1, 'בחגך' was the source for the rule. רב אשי took the rule from a different word. So the גמרא needs to find a new job for 'בחגך' in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (what does he learn from it)
'In your festival' (from the פסוק)

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi,
this word 'in your festival', what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אָשֵׁי, הַאי ״בְּחַגֶּךָ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רב אשי's view from step 2 in light of step 1's use of 'בחגך'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'בחגך' teaches according to רב אשי

steps.title: 'בחגך' teaches no weddings during the מועד
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי uses 'בחגך' for רב's teaching: rejoice in your festival and not with your wife. So one does not marry on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is used for רב דניאל בר קטינא's teaching. רב דניאל בר קטינא said in the name of רב: How do we know that we do not marry women during the מועד? Because it says 'and you shall rejoice in your festival', and not in your wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רב אשי uses 'בחגך' as the source that weddings are not held during חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to rejoice 'in your festival'. רב reads this as: only in your festival, and not in your wife. This gives 'בחגך' its own lesson, so רב אשי's approach holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: For the teaching of רב (like what רב said)
From where do we know?
Marrying women
Here: חול המועד, the middle days of the festival
As it says (introducing a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources for excluding birds and מנחות from festival שמחה: 'בחגך' (step 1) or 'ושמחת' (רב אשי). For רב אשי, 'בחגך' teaches that weddings are not held on חול המועד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for the practical הלכה that weddings are not held on חול המועד.

phrases.english: That word is for the teaching of Rav Daniel bar Ketina.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב דָּנִיאֵל בַּר קַטִּינָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: As Rav Daniel bar Ketina said that Rav said:
From where do we know that one does not marry women during the festival?
As it says: 'And you shall rejoice in your festival,'
and not in your wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בחגך' teaches רב's rule: rejoice in your festival and not in your wife, so no weddings on חול המועד.

steps.title: How to divide offerings between שלמים and עולות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches: if you have many people to feed and little money, bring more שלמים and fewer עולות. If you have much money and few people to feed, bring more עולות and fewer שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who has many people to eat and little property brings many שלמים and few עולות. If he has much property and few people to eat, he brings many עולות and few שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives practical advice on how a person should split his festival offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שלמים is mostly eaten by the owner and his household, while an עולה is burned completely on the מזבח. So a big family with little money should put more into שלמים to feed everyone. Someone with plenty of money and a small household can give more to עולות.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a משנה)
Eaters: people in his household who will eat
Property, money
Peace offerings, mostly eaten by the owners
Burnt offerings, burned completely on the מזבח
Many / few

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who has many eaters
phrases.notes: 'Eaters' means the people in his household who will eat the meat.

phrases.english: and little property —
brings many peace offerings and few burnt offerings.
Much property and few eaters —
brings many burnt offerings and few peace offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אוֹכְלִים מְרוּבִּים וּנְכָסִים מוּעָטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divide festival offerings by household size and money: many eaters means more שלמים, more money means more עולות.

steps.title: The משנה's last two cases: little of both, or much of both
steps.stepSummary: If both money and eaters are few, he brings the minimum amounts. If both are many, he gives generously, according to the blessing he received.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both are few, about him the earlier rule applies: a silver מעה for the עולה and two silver coins for the חגיגה. If both are many, about him the פסוק says: 'Each man as he is able to give, according to the blessing of ה׳ your God which He gave you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of cases. It covers a person with little money and few eaters, and a person with much money and many eaters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 covered the mixed cases, where one is many and the other is few. Here, if both are small, he only has to meet the minimum amounts set at the start of the מסכתא. If both are large, the תורה expects him to give in proportion to his wealth.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that: both his money and his eaters
Few, little
Many, a lot
A silver מעה, the minimum value for the עולת ראיה
According to what his hand can give, meaning as he is able

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה sets four cases. Mixed cases decide which offering gets more. If both are few, he brings the minimum. If both are many, he gives generously according to his blessing.

phrases.english: If both this and that are few —
about this one it was said:
one silver מעה, two silver coins.
phrases.notes: This points back to the first משנה of the מסכתא, which set these minimum amounts for the עולה and the חגיגה.

phrases.english: If both this and that are many —
about this one it was said:
'Each man as he is able to give,

phrases.aramaic: כְּבִרְכַּת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לָךְ״.
phrases.english: according to the blessing of ה׳ your God which He gave you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's list of cases begun in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If both are few, he brings the minimum amounts. If both are many, he gives according to his wealth.

steps.title: How can a poor person bring many שלמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how someone with little money can bring 'many שלמים', since he cannot afford them.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'Many שלמים'? Where does he bring them from? He doesn't have the money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and questions the משנה's first mixed case. A person with many eaters and little money is told to bring many שלמים, but how can he pay for them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to ask the impossible. This person's whole problem is that he has little money, so the גמרא wants to know what source of funds the משנה has in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he bring it?
But he doesn't have it!
Peace offerings, whose meat the owners eat

phrases.english: גמרא:
'Many שלמים.'
From where does he bring them?
He doesn't have the money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by questioning the משנה's case from Step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source of money lets a poor person bring many שלמים?

steps.title: רב חסדא: he combines funds and buys one big bull
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says he combines his own money with other money and buys one large bull, which gives a lot of meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: He combines the money and brings a large bull.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The person adds his own small amount of money to other money he has, such as מעשר שני money, and buys one big bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Many שלמים' does not have to mean many animals. One very large bull also produces plenty of meat for many eaters. Combining the funds makes this affordable.

keyTerms.meaning: Combines, adds one fund to another
A large bull

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
He combines and brings a large bull.
phrases.notes: He means he adds his own money to his מעשר שני money and buys one big animal with both.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: טוֹפֵל וּמֵבִיא פַּר גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He combines his money with other money and buys one large bull.

steps.title: רב ששת: they said one combines animal with animal
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת responds that the Sages said one may combine an animal with an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to him: But they said one may combine an animal with an animal!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת reacts to רב חסדא by quoting a rule about combining animals with animals. His point is not yet clear, and the גמרא will work it out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote is short and could be read two ways. It might limit combining to animals only, or it might add that combining can bring more animals too. The next steps decide which reading is right.

keyTerms.meaning: But they (the Sages) said
One combines an animal with an animal

phrases.english: רב ששת said to him:
But they said:
one combines an animal with an animal!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב חסדא's answer in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's suggestion of one large bull
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule about combining animals with animals seems to say something about how far combining goes, but its exact point is unclear.

steps.title: What did רב ששת mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב ששת was telling רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was he saying to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what רב ששת's remark means. This is a setup line for the two readings that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'one combines an animal with an animal' can be read as a limit or as an addition. The גמרא is about to test each reading.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying to him?

phrases.english: What is he saying to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רב ששת's remark in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was רב ששת limiting רב חסדא or adding to him?

steps.title: Not a limit, or he would have said so plainly
steps.stepSummary: If רב ששת meant 'only animals, not money', he would simply have said 'one does not combine money with money.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he meant: they said one combines an animal with an animal, but not money with money, then he should have just said: one does not combine money with money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first reading, that רב ששת was limiting combining to animals only. It rejects this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב ששת's point were that money cannot be combined, the clear way to say it would be 'one may not combine money with money.' He did not say that, so his words must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
Money with money
Then let him just say to him

phrases.english: If you say this is what he was telling him:
they said one combines an animal with an animal
but not money with money,
then let him just say to him:
one does not combine money with money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible reading of רב ששת.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that רב ששת meant combining is allowed only for animals
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If so, he should have said it directly: 'one does not combine money with money.'

steps.title: He meant: you may even combine and bring more animals
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת meant that the Sages even allowed combining an animal with an animal, so the poor man need not stop at one bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he said to him: they said one may even combine an animal with an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading. רב ששת was adding to רב חסדא, not limiting him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת agrees that combining is allowed. He adds that one may also combine animal with animal: one animal bought with his own money and another bought with מעשר שני money. So why did רב חסדא speak only of one large bull?

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the correct reading)
Even, also

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not arguing that combining money is forbidden. The word אַף shows he is adding a further option, not taking one away.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he said to him:
they said:
one may even combine an animal with an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading after Step 11 rejected the first one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ששת meant one may even combine and bring more animals, not only one large bull.

steps.title: Whose view is רב ששת following?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view רב ששת follows, since it seems to match neither חזקיה nor רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom? Not like חזקיה and not like רבי יוחנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's view. It does not fit either of two known opinions about combining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת allows both kinds of combining, money with money and animal with animal. Earlier, חזקיה allowed only animal with animal and רבי יוחנן allowed only money with money, so רב ששת's broad view seems to have no source.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion is this?
An אמורא who allows combining only an animal with an animal, not money with money
An אמורא who allows combining only money with money, not an animal with an animal

phrases.english: Like whom?
Not like חזקיה
and not like רבי יוחנן!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? דְּלָא כְּחִזְקִיָּה וּדְלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the meaning of רב ששת reached in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's view that both kinds of combining are allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Neither חזקיה nor רבי יוחנן seems to allow both kinds of combining, so רב ששת's view seems to follow no known opinion.

steps.title: Maybe רב ששת holds his own view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests an answer to step 13: only the אמוראים argue, while the ברייתות do not, so רב ששת is free to hold his own in-between view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: it is the אמוראים who argue, but the ברייתות do not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way out: רב ששת does not have to follow חזקיה or רבי יוחנן, because the ברייתות themselves do not argue. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה and רבי יוחנן each brought a ברייתא to support their view. If those ברייתות can be read so that they agree, then the argument is only between the אמוראים. In that case a third אמורא like רב ששת may take his own position.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a suggested answer
The אמוראים, the sages of the גמרא
The ברייתות, teachings from the time of the משנה
They argue / disagree

phrases.english: And if you would say:
it is the amoraim who disagree,
phrases.notes: He means חזקיה and רבי יוחנן from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: but the baraitot do not disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The argument is only between the אמוראים, so a third view is possible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת must follow either חזקיה or רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות agree, so רב ששת may hold his own view

steps.title: A ברייתא says the first eating must be from חולין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion with a ברייתא that says the first eating must come from חולין. This seems to say that money may not be mixed even for one animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches: the first eating is from חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 14 by quoting a ברייתא. That ברייתא seems to clash with רב ששת's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first animal must be fully חולין, then mixing is allowed only for later animals. That would forbid mixing money for one animal, so the ברייתא seems to take a clear side against רב ששת's in-between view.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches: introduces a challenge from a source
The first eating of the offering
Regular money or food that is not holy, unlike מעשר שני

phrases.english: But it teaches:
The first eating is from non-sacred property.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָתָנֵי: אֲכִילָה רִאשׁוֹנָה מִן הַחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתות do not take a side against רב ששת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first eating must be entirely חולין, money cannot be mixed for even one animal, which goes against רב ששת's view.

steps.title: Only the value of the first eating must be חולין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'first eating' means only the value of the required eating amount must come from חולין. The rest of the animal may be paid for with מעשר שני money.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'the first eating'? The money value of the amount needed for the first eating must be from חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא more narrowly. Only part of the first animal's cost has to be חולין money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not require the whole first animal to be חולין. Only the value of the required eating amount must be. So money can be mixed inside one animal, and the ברייתא no longer goes against רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of
The required amount or measure
The money value of

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, 'the first eating from חולין' means only the value of the required eating amount must be חולין money. This leaves room for רב ששת's view.

phrases.english: What is 'the first eating'?
The money value of the required amount of the first eating
phrases.notes: Only that part has to be paid with regular money. The rest of the animal can come from מעשר שני money.

phrases.english: is from non-sacred money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by explaining the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrow reading of the ברייתא's words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole first animal must be bought with חולין money
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the value of the required eating amount must be חולין, so money may be mixed

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the leftover five may be brought on the second day
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes ריש לקיש: if someone set aside ten animals for his חגיגה and brought five on the first day of יום טוב, he may bring the other five on the second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of ריש לקיש: if someone set aside ten animals for his חגיגה and brought five on the first day of יום טוב, he may go back and bring five on the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. ריש לקיש rules that leftover חגיגה animals may still be brought on a later day of the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person did not bring all his animals on the first day. ריש לקיש says that is fine, and he can finish bringing the rest on the next day.

keyTerms.meaning: He set aside (for an offering)
The festival peace-offering
The first day of the festival
He goes back and brings (more offerings)

phrases.english: Ulla said that Reish Lakish said:
If one separated ten animals for his Festival peace-offering,
and he sacrificed five on the first day of the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: חוֹזֵר וּמַקְרִיב חָמֵשׁ בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי.
phrases.english: he may return and sacrifice five on the second day of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the חגיגה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover set-aside חגיגה animals may be brought on a later day of the festival.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: once he stopped, he brings no more
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן argues: once the person stopped bringing offerings, he may not bring the rest on another day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: since he stopped, he may no longer bring offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite ruling from ריש לקיש. Stopping ends his chance to bring the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the moment the person stopped bringing offerings matters. After that point the remaining animals cannot be brought on a later day.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he stopped
He may no longer bring offerings

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Since he stopped,
he may no longer sacrifice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite ruling from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once he stopped bringing offerings, he cannot bring the remaining animals on a later day.

steps.title: רבי אבא: two different cases, so no real argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן do not really argue. One speaks about a case where the person said nothing about his plan, and the other about a case where he spelled out his plan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: they do not argue. Here it is a plain case, and there it is a case where he spelled it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא settles the argument by saying each sage is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a plain case, where he said nothing, we assume he meant to bring everything on the first day, so stopping ends it, as רבי יוחנן said. If he said from the start that he would bring them over several days, he may continue, as ריש לקיש said.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not argue
Here... there: each opinion is about a different case
Plain, without saying what he planned
Spelling out his plan clearly

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבא: if the person did not say his plan, stopping ends the offerings (רבי יוחנן). If he said he would bring them over several days, he may continue (ריש לקיש).
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבא's words do not say which 'here' goes with which sage, but the next steps make it clear: the plain case is the one where stopping ends the offerings (רבי יוחנן), and the spelled-out case is the one where he may continue (ריש לקיש).

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said: And they do not disagree:
Here it is where he did not specify, there it is where he specified.
phrases.notes: Specified means he said from the start that he would bring the animals over the festival days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the argument between steps 17 and 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each sage speaks about a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about the same case
steps.terutzMaskana: A plain case follows רבי יוחנן, and a spelled-out case follows ריש לקיש
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether he may finish bringing the offerings depends on whether he spelled out from the start that he would bring them over several days.

steps.title: What is the 'said nothing' case? Not a case of running out of time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the סתם case is, where רבי יוחנן says he may not bring the rest. It cannot be a case where there was no time left in the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly is this case where he did not say anything? If you say there was no time left in the day to bring them all, then it is clear why he did not bring them: there was no time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the סתם case looks like, where רבי יוחנן forbids bringing the rest. It tries a first possibility, that he ran out of time, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן forbids bringing the rest because stopping shows he gave up on them. But if he stopped only because the day ran out, stopping shows nothing about his plan. So that cannot be the case where it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Plain, unspecified: he did not say what he planned
What are the circumstances? What does the case look like?
If you say (the first suggestion)
Enough time left in the day

phrases.english: This case of 'not specified,' what are the circumstances?
If we say that there is no time left in the day to sacrifice,
then this, that he did not sacrifice them,
is because there was no time in the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the סתם case in רבי אבא's answer (Step 19) looks like.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case of 'said nothing' would make רבי יוחנן forbid bringing the remaining animals?

steps.title: Not a case of having no one to eat the meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a second possibility, that he did not have enough people to eat the meat, and rejects it for the same reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say he did not have enough people to eat the meat. But then it is clear why he did not bring them: he had no one to eat them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second picture of the סתם case and rejects it too. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat of a חגיגה must be eaten in time, so a person without enough eaters holds back to avoid leftovers. Here too, stopping has a clear outside reason and does not show he gave up on the animals.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather (moving to another possibility)
Eaters: people to eat the offering's meat

phrases.english: But rather, where he does not have eaters,
then this, that he did not sacrifice them,
is because he does not have eaters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second possible case, rejected the same way as the first.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Could the סתם case be one where he lacked people to eat the meat?

steps.title: The case: he had time and eaters, so he left them on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The סתם case is where he had both time and eaters and still did not bring the rest. That shows he left them on purpose, so he may not bring them later.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ruling is needed for a case where there was time in the day and he had people to eat. Since he did not bring them on the first day anyway, we learn that he left them on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The forbidden סתם case is one where nothing stopped him, yet he did not bring the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no outside reason for stopping, the only explanation is his own choice. His silence plus his stopping counts as deciding to leave the animals. So רבי יוחנן says he cannot bring them on a later day.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for… (this case)
Learn from it, conclude from this
He deliberately left them over

steps.whatToRemember: In the סתם case, a person who had time and eaters but still stopped is treated as having left the remaining animals on purpose.

phrases.english: No, it is needed only
where there is time in the day
and he has eaters;
from the fact that he did not sacrifice them on the first day,
learn from it that he deliberately left them over.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִיכָּא שְׁהוּת בַּיּוֹם וְאִית לֵיהּ אוֹכְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Steps 20-21 after rejecting both possibilities.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The סתם case is when there was time and eaters, so stopping shows he left them on purpose.

steps.title: Support: רבין reports that רבי יוחנן allows bringing the rest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי אבא's answer makes sense. רבין reports that רבי יוחנן himself allows bringing the other five animals on the second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if a person set aside ten animals for his חגיגה and brought five on the first day of יום טוב, he may go back and bring five on the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing support for רבי אבא's answer. It quotes a second report of רבי יוחנן that says the opposite of עולא's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18, רבי יוחנן said that once he stops, he may not bring the rest. Now רבין reports רבי יוחנן saying he may bring them. This sets up a clash inside רבי יוחנן's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is reasonable (support is coming)
When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
He set aside (animals for an offering)
He goes back and sacrifices

phrases.english: And so too it is reasonable,
for when רבין came
he said that רבי יוחנן said:
If one set aside ten animals for his festival offering,
and sacrificed five on the first day of the festival,

phrases.aramaic: חוֹזֵר וּמַקְרִיב חָמֵשׁ בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי.
phrases.english: he may go back and sacrifice five on the second day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּכִי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a proof for רבי אבא's answer from Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבא's answer that the 'forbidden' and 'allowed' rulings speak about different cases.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין's report of רבי יוחנן allowing the remaining five animals on the second day.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's two statements clash
steps.stepSummary: עולא's report and רבין's report of רבי יוחנן contradict each other. This sets up the proof that רבי יוחנן must be speaking about two different cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: These two statements contradict each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוחנן's two reported rulings clash. This prepares the next move, which will resolve the clash in a way that supports רבי אבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In one report רבי יוחנן forbids bringing the rest, and in the other he allows it. The clash is the heart of the proof: the easiest way out is that one ruling is about a person who said nothing, and the other about one who spelled out his plan.

keyTerms.meaning: They contradict each other

steps.confusionAlert: This contradiction is not an attack on רבי אבא. It is the tool that proves him right, because it shows רבי יוחנן himself must split the cases.

phrases.english: They contradict each other.
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן's ruling in עולא's report (Step 18) and his ruling in רבין's report.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רבין's report next to עולא's report and points out that they clash.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two reports of רבי יוחנן's ruling (Step 18 and Step 23).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One report forbids bringing the remaining animals and the other allows it, so they cannot both be true for the same case.

steps.title: Two different cases: unspecified versus clearly stated
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is solved by saying that רבי יוחנן was talking about two different cases. In the סתם case he forbids bringing the rest later. In the מפרש case he allows it. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we must conclude that one ruling is about a case where he did not say anything, and the other is about a case where he said his plan clearly. Yes, conclude this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction from the last step. It says the two reports of רבי יוחנן are about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's report, which says he may not bring the rest, is about the סתם case: he had time and people to eat and still left them, so he left them on purpose. רבין's report, which says he may bring them, is about the מפרש case, where he said from the start that he would bring the rest later. The closing words 'שמע מינה' mean the גמרא accepts this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that... (opens the only answer left)
Without saying anything; he left his plan unstated
Saying it clearly; he stated his plan out loud
Learn from it; conclude this

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, if a person said nothing and skipped animals he could have brought, he may not bring them on a later day. If he clearly said he would bring them later, he may.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן changed his mind or that one report is wrong. Both reports are correct, because each one is about a different case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the standard way the גמרא handles two rulings from the same אמורא that seem to clash: it shows they are about different cases.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this:
here, where he did not specify,
phrases.notes: This is עולא's report, which says he may not bring the rest.

phrases.english: there, where he stated it explicitly.
phrases.notes: This is רבין's report, which allows bringing the other animals on the second day.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כָּאן בִּסְתָם כָּאן בִּמְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the contradiction raised in step 24 by giving each report its own case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן forbids bringing the leftover animals later in the סתם case and allows it in the מפרש case.

steps.title: Another report of רבי יוחנן is introduced as support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins bringing another report, from רב שמן בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן, to support the split between סתם and מפרש. The report itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also said: רב שמן בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to quote another teaching of רבי יוחנן that backs up the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'איתמר נמי' tell us that what follows will support the conclusion we just reached, from a separate report of רבי יוחנן. The actual words of רבי יוחנן come right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated; this introduces support for what was just said
An אמורא who reports a teaching in the name of רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rav Shemen bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a supporting report for the conclusion reached in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The split in step 25 between the סתם case and the מפרש case
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of רבי יוחנן reported by רב שמן בר אבא (quoted in the following text)
